predictions.reasoning: From the added facts: Brock does not enjoy horror. From the new rule: if Brock enjoyed horror he would both appreciate darkness and explore morality; since he does not enjoy horror, this rule is irrelevant and gives no information about whether he appreciates darkness or explores morality. From the added facts: Brock either admires Damon or likes vampires (but not necessarily exclusively). Also: Brock either prefers Stefan or admires Damon, but not both. So exactly one of {prefers Stefan, admires Damon} is true. Combining: suppose Brock admires Damon. Then the second disjunction is satisfied (he does not prefer Stefan), and the first disjunction (admires Damon or likes vampires) is satisfied regardless of whether he likes vampires. So admiring Damon is consistent. Suppose instead Brock does not admire Damon. Then from the first disjunction he must like vampires. From the second disjunction, since he does not admire Damon, he must prefer Stefan. So Brock may either admire Damon (and not prefer Stefan) or not admire Damon (and prefer Stefan). Both scenarios are logically consistent with the context. Therefore the context does not force Brock to prefer Stefan; it merely allows it. Hence the entailment does not hold.
